question: Should OpenClaw adopt this repository-wide localization registry and generated coverage manifest as a required cross-surface governance contract, or keep localization ownership and checks scoped to existing surface-specific implementations?
rationale: The branch creates a new shared package, environment-driven locale behavior, a checked inventory, and a required check lane across multiple owners; choosing the permanent contract and rollout boundary is product and ownership policy, not a mechanical repair.

options.title: Sponsor an owner-published shared contract
options.body: Keep the generic core schema and owner/domain declarations, but require documented locale-setting and upgrade behavior plus real check evidence before the dependent series is landed.

options.title: Constrain the scope to existing surfaces
options.body: Retain only narrowly needed contributor guidance or per-surface checks and defer the shared registry and release-governance layer until a maintainer-approved design exists.

options.title: Pause the series pending RFC approval
options.body: Keep the drafts open but do not merge cumulative foundation slices until the linked RFC establishes ownership, compatibility, and release policy.

recommendation.title: Sponsor an owner-published shared contract
recommendation.body: Keep the generic core schema and owner/domain declarations, but require documented locale-setting and upgrade behavior plus real check evidence before the dependent series is landed.

likelyOwner.reason: The available context identifies this person as the author of the RFC-linked series and the ownership-refactor follow-up; a repository owner should make the final sponsorship decision.
